svg.title: Ten Core Seats; Two Explicit Scale Additions
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-ten-to-twelve-person-pod; chart type: org_architecture; title: Ten Core Seats; Two Explicit Scale Additions; subtitle: Base and Conservative: 7 FT + 3 C. Scaled: 8 FT + 4 C.; chapter number: 11; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Each numeric value represents one person. The first ten seats form the core pod; the final two activate only in the Scaled case. Contractors are people, not full-time-equivalent claims. Roles are an illustrative combined ownership-and-operation roster, not ten extra hires above an acquired workforce.; caption: The acquisition lead owns capital allocation; the general manager directs operations. Specialist contractors support defined workstreams without replacing management accountability.; stages: label: Acquisition lead; value: Core FT 1 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own purchase discipline, lender relationships, investment decisions, seller negotiations, and the weekly review of liquidity and customer concentration.; label: General manager; value: Core FT 2 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own the operating result, customer retention, staffing priorities, service recovery, and execution of the post-close 100-day integration plan.; label: Operations lead; value: Core FT 3 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Control scheduling, vendor commitments, capacity allocation, backlog aging, and daily escalation of delivery constraints to the general manager.; label: Service lead; value: Core FT 4 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Set delivery standards, supervise job execution, review defects, and preserve customer-specific operating knowledge that could leave with the seller.; label: Delivery specialist; value: Core FT 5 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Perform customer work, capture completion evidence, record materials and hours, and flag scope changes before they become unbilled service.; label: Account and retention lead; value: Core FT 6 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own renewals, customer transition calls, dispute resolution, concentration monitoring, and early escalation of threatened account departures.; label: Controller and reporting lead; value: Core FT 7 of 7; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Own QuickBooks reconciliations, the cash forecast, receivables follow-up, covenant calculations, and automated management reporting with reviewed exceptions.; label: Transaction counsel; value: Core contractor 1 of 3; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review transaction disclosures, purchase terms, lien releases, license transfers, employment issues, and post-close claims within a defined engagement.; label: QoE and tax specialist; value: Core contractor 2 of 3; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Normalize earnings, test working capital, evaluate tax allocation, and reconcile diligence findings with the opening operating-company records.; label: Systems and workflow specialist; value: Core contractor 3 of 3; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Configure Microsoft 365 access, accounting integrations, backups, and back-office workflows; document recovery procedures and test exception ownership.; label: Capacity supervisor; value: Scaled addition: FT 8 of 8; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Add only in the twelve-person Scaled configuration to supervise higher throughput, absorb scheduling complexity, and prevent service-quality erosion.; label: Integration coach; value: Scaled addition: contractor 4 of 4; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Add time-bounded process coaching and integration support in the Scaled configuration; transfer documented routines to the permanent operating leads.
